checks.upstream_pattern: RISCVInstrInfoXpulp.td:51/61: the parser classes become UImmAsmOperand<12/5,"PCRel">, the same mechanism as upstream simm13_lsb0 (SImmAsmOperand<13,"Lsb0">, RISCVInstrInfo.td ~271 at llvmorg-20.1.8, used by CV_BEQIMM in RISCVInstrInfoXCV.td:506). RISCVAsmParser.cpp:725 isBareSymbolOrUImm<N> copies isBareSimmNLsb0 (upstream RISCVAsmParser.cpp:523) line for line, with isUInt<N> in place of isShiftedInt<N-1,1>. That substitution is right: these fields are unsigned, and a constant is the raw halfword field value, which is the existing LLVM behaviour. The printer, decoder and encoder are unchanged.
checks.count_operand: The change is correct and needed. LOOP{0,1}setupi $uimmL and LOOP{0,1}counti $uimmL are trip counts. Their users only ever add immediates (PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp:819-827 .addImm; the setupi builders in PULPHardwareLoops.cpp). GNU as rejects a label there ('lp.counti requires absolute expression'). One correction to the task framing: the old declaration did NOT accept a label as a count. On int-20, 'lp.counti x0, .Lx' crashes ('Unknown match type detected!') like the other forms. The old uimm12pcrel on the count was a wrong declaration that could not be reached, because its parser class was constant-only. It had to change so that the new PCRel class does not let a label into the count field, where getMachineOpValue would encode a distance as the trip count. The fork's uimm12 (RISCVInstrInfo.td:270, fork-defined) has the same 12-bit field and decodeUImmOperand<12>. Its getImmOpValue returns MO.getImm() for immediates, the same as the old default getMachineOpValue, so encodings do not change. It also adds OPERAND_UIMM12 machine-verifier range checking, which ImmLeaf already guarantees. Verified on 20-F010: 'lp.counti x0, .Lx' and 'lp.setupi x0, .Lx, .Lx' are rejected with '[0, 4095]'.
checks.backend_checks: RISCVAsmBackend.cpp:523-541 adds a range check (isUInt<13>/isUInt<6> of the byte distance) and a 2-byte alignment check with reportError, as upstream does for fixup_riscv_branch (RISCVAsmBackend.cpp:461-464 at 20.1.8). The return value (Value >> 1) is unchanged. Boundary run against GAP9 riscv32-unknown-elf-as -march=rv32imcxgap9 (.option norvc, target at distance d): lp.setupi d=4/60/62 both accept with identical .text; d=64/66/104 both reject (GNU 'BFD_RELOC_RISCV_RELU5 Overflow'). lp.setup d=4/8190 identical; 8192/8194 both reject (REL12 Overflow). lp.endi x0 / lp.starti x1: 8190 identical, 8192 both reject. Backward labels: both reject. Zero distance: both accept with identical bytes. The only difference is an odd distance (63 / 8191): LLVM gives 'fixup value must be 2-byte aligned', while GNU as silently truncates (63 encodes as 31 halfwords). Rejecting is the upstream fixup_riscv_branch behaviour, and a loop end on an odd address is impossible in valid RV code, so this is benign stricter checking.

notes_for_conductor: The two commits must land together: 9e4f849a6239 alone does not build, because the generated matcher references isUImm12PCRel/isUImm5PCRel from daf52f7bbc58. After autosquash, the insn-tablegen cluster commit will not build without the mc cluster commit above it. This is acceptable if the stack is only built at its tip, but it is worth recording.

Pre-existing divergences recorded by the worker and confirmed: GNU as treats a numeric label operand as a byte offset, while LLVM treats it as a raw halfword field ('lp.setupi x0,10,32' is an LLVM range error and accepted by GNU). GNU as silently truncates odd distances, which LLVM now rejects. GNU as emits R_RISCV_REL12/RELU5 relocations that ld.lld cannot link. These are owner-decision items for BACKLOG.md, not F010 defects.
